doc_friction.issue: The queue listed 1,243 alerts from a scan of e98ec5cbb, older than PR 18676's fixes; 1,189 were in files already changed. Nothing in the alert file said which commit was scanned, so a session would redo fixes. Fixed in this PR (step 0).
platform/security/risk_review.py crashes with CalledProcessError when origin/main is a depth-1 fetch (merge-base fails); a git fetch --deepen=50 origin main was needed first.

PR 18806 (same fix, another session) merged while this PR waited about 40 minutes for CI. The duplicate check before opening found nothing because 18806 was opened after it. The merge conflict was the only signal.

deviations.why: Step 0 says take the top alert and fix it. Alert #1 was already fixed on main (PR 18676), and so were 1,189 of 1,243 queued alerts.
deviations.did: Fixed the queue generator so alerts name their scan commit and get a still-there check, instead of re-fixing code. Routed --track process for the record. Narrowed to a shallow-safe step 0 after PR 18806 landed the rest.

deviations.why: No customer post: this is internal security-queue tooling with no customer-facing angle.
deviations.did: Wrote an agent doc in docs/reports/ instead.

notes: CodeQL main run 45521750254 (e98ec5cbb) took 64 min; 12 later main runs were cancelled while pending. Run 45529454613 on 5f857bb81 (after PR 18676) was in progress at about 02:10 UTC, so the queue should shrink to about 54 when it finishes. Possible false positives left open: js/incomplete-hostname-regexp in test strings and XML namespace URIs (see report). Tests: test_security_alerts 16 OK. risk_review: blocked on nothing. After a conflict with PR 18806 (same idea, merged first), I kept main's version and narrowed this PR to a shallow-safe step 0 (fetch the full SHA, then diff).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
